titulo: Weekly and monthly cadence and the Plan B for days 30 to 60
lead: SEO pays off in weeks and months, not days. What makes the result is the routine: one look per week, one battery of checks per month and, between days 30 and 60, an answer for each symptom instead of giving up. And one precaution almost nobody takes: Search Console keeps only about 16 months. If you don't archive, you lose your own history.
objetivo: set up the weekly and monthly routine, archive the history and choose the right answer for each symptom from days 30 to 60.

aprende.t: The cadence: week 0, each page, weekly, monthly
Plan B: one symptom, one answer
Practice in a simulated conversation and build the dated plan

hero_alt: A wall calendar with dates circled in pencil, next to a compass and a closed laptop.

nos.detalhe: Foundation done (course 1) and measurement turned on: baseline, brand regex, key URLs, conversion goal (lessons 1, 2, 3 and 7).
Quality checklist, 2 or 3 old pages pointing to the new one, and a notice to search engines only with a URL that returns 200.
Non-branded export, inspection of the key URLs, pages with impressions and no clicks (lesson 4), queries with no owner page (lesson 5).
20 to 30 fixed questions from your customer, run by hand in 4 or 5 AI assistants, with a spreadsheet of date, assistant, and result. Answers vary; that is why the battery is fixed and repeated.
Each symptom has a likely cause and a response. Giving up is not in the table.
Search Console keeps about 16 months. Save each week in a folder of your own (the resumo.csv and the non-branded files). The gsc-historico tool puts everything into a local database.

secoes.volta: What got stuck during the week goes back to the decision list
secoes.legenda: A little each week, always. This routine is what separates signal from scare.

texto: Pick a fixed day and time. Run the export (or the spreadsheet), inspect the key URLs, and write down one decision.
One decision per week is enough: change a title, write a topic, strengthen a page.

exemplo.texto: The weekly report runs every Tuesday morning and only generates files; a person decides and publishes.

texto: Run the same 20 to 30 questions in the same assistants, in an incognito window, and note whether your site appears, with which address, and who appears in its place.
A paid "share of voice" tool is a sample, not an official score. A local model does not measure what the real AIs answer.
Read the symptom before acting: few indexed, indexed with no impressions, impressions with no clicks, position 11 to 30 stalled, a drop after publishing a lot.
Each one has a response in the table below.
Save the resumo.csv and the non-branded files from every week in a folder with a backup.
Next step: the gsc-historico tool imports that folder into a local database that never deletes anything and generates the up, down, and topic report.

secoes.titulo: The Plan B table, the schedule, and the archive
secoes.sub: Replace what is between < > with your own. The gsc-historico commands come from the tool's README; the details of the tool are covered in course 7.

blocos.conteudo:
| symptom (day 30–60) | likely cause | what to do |
|---|---|---|
| few pages indexed | crawling, wrong canonical, thin page | URL Inspection, internal links, noindex on the thin ones, request indexing again |
| indexed, almost no impressions | keyword with no demand or lack of authority | revalidate with Search Console data; change the topic; backlinks |
| impressions with no clicks (CTR < 0.5%) | weak title/description | title with a specific promise and a number; measure for 2 weeks |
| position 11–30 stalled | content ok, low authority | external links to the winners; new sections for the queries that showed up |
| overall drop after publishing a lot | signal of content at scale | stop, audit with the checklist, merge/remove the weak ones, lower cadence |

Every <Tuesday> <9am>: non-branded export + inspection of the key URLs + 1 decision (30 min)
Every day <1>: battery of <25> questions in <4> assistants (1 h)
Day <30> and day <60> after publishing: read the symptom and apply Plan B
Every <Friday>: check that the week went into the archive folder

secoes.titulo: Simulated conversation: the store owner wants to quit on day 45
secoes.sub: Simulated conversation for practice. Pick the answer you would give; the comment appears right after.

abre.cliente: I published 10 pages 45 days ago and nothing happened. I think SEO doesn't work for me. I want to stop.

opcoes.t: Before you decide, let's look at the symptom: how many of the 10 are indexed?
opcoes.comenta: Plan B starts with the symptom. "Nothing happened" can be five different problems, each with its own answer.

opcoes.t: Then publish 50 more pages to make up for it.
opcoes.comenta: Volume doesn't cure a symptom. Publishing a lot at once is the signal of content at scale that takes sites down.

opcoes.t: Relax, SEO takes time. Wait another six months.
opcoes.comenta: Patience is part of SEO, but waiting without looking at anything doesn't teach you what to fix.

espera.cliente: Wait six months without knowing what for? I was offered a service that indexes everything in 24 hours.

opcoes.t: You're right to want to know. Let's check the state of the pages in URL Inspection.
opcoes.comenta: You went back to the symptom, one step behind the direct answer.
A paid indexer is a typical spam tool. The right path is sitemap, inspection and IndexNow.

indexacao.cliente: I checked: 8 of the 10 are indexed. Impressions showed up from people who didn't search for my brand, but zero clicks.

opcoes.t: Good sign. Before changing anything, let's see which queries the impressions come from and at what position.
opcoes.comenta: Non-branded impressions are the first sign. The position tells you whether the title matters or the problem is something else.

opcoes.t: Then change all the titles today.
opcoes.comenta: It could be the answer, but without seeing queries and position it's a guess. And changing everything at once keeps you from measuring.

opcoes.t: Zero clicks is a failure. Delete the pages.
opcoes.comenta: You threw away the first sign. At INEMA, non-branded started exactly like this: impressions rising and 0 clicks.

posicao.cliente: The non-branded queries are between positions 30 and 60.

opcoes.t: Indexed content, low authority: links back to the best pages and new sections for the queries that showed up.
opcoes.comenta: That's the "stuck position" line of Plan B. The content got in; it lacks the strength to climb.
Switching topics is the answer for indexed with no impressions. Here there are impressions: the topic has demand.

opcoes.t: Rewrite the titles to raise the CTR.
opcoes.comenta: At position 30 to 60 almost nobody sees the title. Rewriting isn't bad, it just doesn't solve this symptom (lesson 4).

arquivo.cliente: Agreed. And how will I know, a year and a half from now, whether it improved?

opcoes.t: By saving the export every week in a folder of your own. Search Console only keeps about 16 months.
opcoes.comenta: A weekly archive is the only way to compare beyond 16 months.

opcoes.t: Just open the dashboard, it keeps everything.
opcoes.comenta: It doesn't. After about 16 months, the early data is gone.

fim-escala.texto: She published 50 similar pages and the new ones stalled at "Discovered – currently not indexed". The original symptom was still undiagnosed.

fim-indexador.texto: The service promised 24 hours. The page stayed out of the index and the site picked up a risk it didn't have before.

fim-apagou.texto: The pages vanished along with the first non-branded impressions. Starting over costs more than waiting for the click.

fim-titulo.texto: The titles got better, but at position 40 nobody saw them. The position stayed put.

fim-perdeu.texto: A year and a half later, the starting week was no longer in the dashboard. There was no way to prove the improvement.

fim-bom.texto: Symptom read, Plan B response applied, and every week saved. A year and a half from now, the comparison will be in her folder.

secoes.licao: Plan B means reading the symptom before you act: indexing, impressions, position, clicks. And saving every week, because the dashboard forgets.

secoes.titulo: Practice: the routine on your calendar
secoes.sub: Do it once, and it lasts the whole year.

exercicios.texto: Put the template's reminders on your calendar: weekly, monthly, day 30 and day 60 after your next publication.
exercicios.pronto: your calendar has 4 recurring or dated reminders, each with the task written out.

exercicios.texto: Create the archive folder with a backup and save the most recent week in it (summary and non-branded file, or the spreadsheet).
exercicios.pronto: the folder exists, has the 1st week saved with the date in the name, and is in a place with a backup copy.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: The pages are indexed, have impressions, and are stuck between positions 11 and 30. What is the Plan B response?
opcoes: Links back to the best ones and new sections for the queries that showed up.
perguntas.explica: Content is fine, authority is low. Changing the topic is for those with no impressions.

perguntas.p: Why archive the weekly export if the dashboard already shows the numbers?
opcoes: Because Search Console keeps only about 16 months of performance data.
perguntas.explica: After about 16 months, the starting week disappears. Without an archive, there is no way to compare.

perguntas.p: In the monthly battery, why are the questions fixed?
opcoes: Because AI answers vary; with fixed questions, the change comes from the site and not from the question.
perguntas.explica: A question that changes every month measures nothing. Keep it fixed, across 4 or 5 assistants, with a date and a result.

perguntas.p: A general drop right after publishing many pages. What should you do?
opcoes: Stop, audit with the checklist, merge or remove the weak ones, and lower the cadence.
perguntas.explica: It is the sign of content at scale. The response is fewer and better, not more.
